shortlist.label: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse pancreatic enlargement, jaundice, and elevated CA19-9 level

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse pancreatic enlargement, elevated hepatobiliary enzymes, and normal serum IgG4 levels

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of abdominal pain, elevated hepatobiliary enzymes, and pancreatic duct narrowing

shortlist.label: Pancreatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Jaundice, epigastric tenderness, and elevated carcinoembryonic antigen level

shortlist.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic duct dilation and elevated CA19-9 level

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with jaundice, epigastric tenderness, elevated bilirubin, and elevated tumor markers (CEA and CA19-9) along with imaging findings of a diffusely enlarged pancreas and bile duct stenosis are highly suggestive of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
rejected.why: Normal serum IgG4 levels make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis
rejected.why: The presence of significant jaundice and elevated tumor markers are not typical for chronic pancreatitis

rejected.label: Pancreatic cancer
rejected.why: This is a broad term that encompasses several types of pancreatic malignancies, but pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
rejected.why: While this could cause pancreatic enlargement and bile duct dilation, the presence of significantly elevated tumor markers and the pattern of FDG-PET uptake suggest a more aggressive malignancy like pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
